subject: Agriculture
title: The Bengal Famine of 1943
description: One-minute skill: The Bengal Famine of 1943.

hook.text: Three million people died in Bengal in 1943—not because there wasn't enough food, but because of policy.

buildup.text: British wartime policies diverted rice to military supply. Prices spiked beyond what ordinary people could pay.

discovery.text: Economist Amartya Sen showed that most famines aren't about food shortage—they're about access and power.

twist.text: Bengal actually had enough food to feed its population. Distribution failures and hoarding caused the deaths.

climax.text: The Bengal Famine shaped India's post-independence obsession with food self-sufficiency—driving Green Revolution adoption.

punchline.text: Famine can happen with full granaries. Access kills, not scarcity.

quiz.question: What did Amartya Sen conclude about the Bengal Famine?
options: Food was available but access and distribution failures caused the famine
